calendar.window: Continuous / no fixed deadline — worth knowing so you stop waiting for a date
calendar.action: EMBO accepts applications on any day of the year (cutoffs only sort you into rounds). NIST PREP at Gaithersburg/UMD is genuinely rolling — 200 live postings, no closing dates, and Michigan Tech states plainly that PREP positions 'will be posted on a rolling basis'; set a saved search on jobs.colorado.edu for the Boulder hub instead of a calendar date, where open windows have run 14 to 47 days. NIH re-entry supplements (for a career interruption of at least six months and no more than eight years) have NO NIH-wide date — each Institute publishes its own on the ICO Funding Considerations page; the binding date is usually your host IC's current-fiscal-year cut-off (May–July for most), NIEHS runs a dated cycle (1 Feb / 1 Apr / 1 Jun / 1 Sep / 1 Oct / 1 Dec), NIDDK takes them 'at any time', and NCI hard-stops on 31 July. NIH T32 is an appointment your programme makes, not an application you file — ask your training-grant director whether there is a slot, and note trainees must be US citizens, nationals or permanent residents. CIRM Scholars is an application to one of 18 host programmes, each with its own deadline (UCSF ~21 Sept, UCSC ~31 Aug, UCI ~mid-June in the last posted cycles) — and current CIRM EDUC4 grants appear to be in their final year, with no renewal RFA published.

first_moves: DAY 1 — Build your one-page eligibility arithmetic sheet, because more applications die here than in review. Write down: date your PhD was conferred; months of postdoctoral research experience as of each upcoming due date (this is what the K99 4-year rule and the NSF PRFB 15-month rule measure); citizenship or permanent-residency status; months of NRSA support already used at the postdoctoral level including any T32 time (the F32 cap is 3 years aggregate); months you have lived or worked in your host country in the last 18 months and months you have worked with your prospective host supervisor (EMBO and HFSP mobility rules, which AGGREGATE prior short stays); and whether you have ever accepted another postdoctoral fellowship (an absolute bar at Damon Runyon).

DAY 1 — Sort yourself by citizenship before you read another RFA. US citizen / non-citizen national / lawful permanent resident opens NIH F32, the LRP, NSF PRFB/AAPF/MSPRF, and the USDA AFRI postdoc fellowship. Everyone else should skip those entirely and work the K99 (confirm with the IC), EMBO, HFSP, Damon Runyon, AHA, HHMI Hanna Gray, Schmidt, the disease foundations, and CIRM's California programmes, where UCSF states verbatim 'There are no citizenship requirements.'

DAY 2 — Compute your K99 window and put two dates in your calendar, not one. Find the due date at which you will be at ~24–36 months of postdoc: that is your A0 target. Then add ~9 months for the A1 (the A1 cannot be submitted before the A0's summary statement issues, which is what forces an October A0 into a July A1). If your A0 target is already past 44 months, treat the K99 as a single shot and build a second route in parallel. If you work on cancer, stop and confirm your IC first — NCI does not participate in the parent K99/R00.

WEEK 1 — Do the free, immediate, high-yield thing. If you are a US citizen or permanent resident with student debt and take no research support or salary from a for-profit, start the NIH Loan Repayment Program application today: it is open, it closes 19 Nov 2026 at 11:59 p.m. EST, it does not require you to hold NIH funding, and NRSA payback deferral is automatic on acceptance. Its reference letters, mentor letter and Institutional Business Official certification all share that same deadline with no grace period, so request them in week one.

WEEK 1 — If HHMI Hanna Gray is remotely plausible, complete the ARC eligibility questionnaire now (live since 15 Sept 2026). It is the gate: without it the application form does not open to you on 3 Nov, and — more valuable — it unlocks HHMI's redacted REAL applications, which is the best study material any funder on this list publishes.

WEEK 1 — Have one specific conversation with your PI and ask three things, not one. (a) Will they write the sponsor/mentor package, and when? (b) Are they already sponsoring someone else this cycle? Damon Runyon takes one application per sponsor per review session and caps a sponsor at two concurrent Fellows; HFSP allows one LOI endorsement per host supervisor per year; Pew allows one applicant per sponsor per year; AHA caps a mentor at four AHA fellows. A popular lab can simply be full, and you cannot see that from outside. (c) Can they give you their current and pending support, which several applications require.

WEEK 1 — Email one programme officer. For NIH, the IC's training or career-development officer: the parent K99 NOFO says candidates are 'strongly encouraged to obtain confirmation of their eligibility from the relevant IC before they begin to prepare their applications.' For NASA NPP, email the NASA Center advisor named on the research-opportunity listing — their recommendation is a GATE ('Proposals that are recommended by the advisor, move on to the external review phase'), and they may not serve as one of your three referees.

WEEK 2 — Register in the portals now, because the registrations, not the writing, are what run out of time. eRA Commons plus an ORCID iD (required for the F32, and required for the LRP since 1 Sept 2026); Research.gov as an Individual Researcher, and FIX YOUR ADDRESS there, because NSF's 5 p.m. 'local time' is keyed to it and changes need 21 days; ProposalCentral (Damon Runyon, AHA, BWF, ALS Association, HFSP); Zintellect (NASA NPP); eBRAP plus Grants.gov Workspace (CDMRP); SmartSimple (TRDRP, MSCRF, some CIRM hosts); ARC (HHMI); Fluxx (RSF, Blood Cancer United); ACLS OFA. NIH warns that registration 'can take 6 weeks or more.'

WEEK 2 — Start the two slowest assets: a SciENcv NIH Biographical Sketch (first build is slow, then reusable everywhere) and a one-page Specific Aims. The Aims page is the single most reusable object you own — it becomes the NSF project summary, the Damon Runyon 5-page proposal's spine, the foundation abstract, and the thing you send a programme officer to get a five-minute read.

WEEK 2 — Pick exactly two targets for this cycle and one for next, and write the sequencing rule down: which offer you would accept first if two landed, and what that would close. Applying broadly is correct; accepting carelessly is what ends a route permanently.
who_to_talk_to: NIH Institute/Center programme officer (the training or career-development contact named in the NOFO) — 3–6 months before the due date, not two weeks. Ask: does this IC accept this mechanism on this cycle (for T32 the answer is often 'January council only'); do I meet the 4-year K99 clock as YOU count it; which study section is likely; and — specific to autumn 2026 — whether NOT-OD-26-114's reduced-discussion review (30–35% of applications discussed instead of ~50%) extends beyond the January 2027 council to the May 2027 council that an October 2026 K submission feeds. NIH has not announced this either way; that is a genuine unknown, not something you are failing to find.

Your NASA Center advisor, for NPP — FIRST, before you write the proposal. The advisor's recommendation gates entry to external review, the research-opportunity listing names them, and they cannot be one of your three reference letters. Contact them months before the 1 November deadline.

Your prospective sponsoring scientist for the NSF fellowships — at least 6–8 weeks out. PRFB requires a 3-page Sponsoring Scientist Statement that YOU upload; MSPRF the same; AAPF needs a host-institution letter carrying BOTH the department chair's and the proposed mentor's signatures. Ask explicitly whether they will also be a reference — for PRFB the sponsor should NOT be, and for MSPRF the sponsoring scientist may not write a reference letter unless they were your doctoral adviser.

Your sponsored-projects / research office — in week one, even for awards you submit yourself. Tell them which of your applications are SELF-SUBMITTED (NSF fellowships, EMBO, HFSP LOI, NASA NPP, Damon Runyon, most foundations) so nobody waits for a routing form, and get the internal deadline in writing for the ones the AOR does submit (NIH), which typically runs 3–5 business days before the NIH date.

Your institution's limited-submission or nominations office — for the awards you cannot enter on your own: Schmidt Science Fellows (partner institutions only; internal nomination ~2 months before the July application, and check the nominating-partner list FIRST because if your PhD institution is not on it there is no route at all), ADA Pathway (two nominations per institution per cycle, one basic/preclinical and one translational — so your real competition is internal), Simons Junior Fellows (nominator required, and either the nominator or the recommender must be external to your institution), SfN NSP, and CIRM Scholars host programmes.

Your Institutional Business Official and financial-aid office — for the LRP certification, several weeks before 19 November. It is a common single point of failure and shares the deadline with everything else: 'Applications that are incomplete — including those missing supplemental information, such as recommendations and institutional certification — as of the applicable deadline will not be considered for further review.'

Two or three PRIOR AWARDEES of the exact mechanism, ideally in your subfield — this is the highest-return hour you will spend, and most funders make them findable. Damon Runyon publishes each Fellow with a lay abstract, institution and NAMED SPONSOR. Pew's Directory of Fellows gives the fellow's institutional email, lab URL, research field, country of origin and mentor, and Pew staff will make introductions directly (fellowsapp@pewtrusts.org). SfN publishes the current NSP cohort. APS names its Blewett selection committee. BWF publishes its CAMS and CASI advisory-committee members by name — the closest thing to a study-section roster you will get outside NIH.

Named programme contacts worth an email, with what to ask: EMBO fellowships@embo.org — any eligibility exception must be agreed BEFORE you submit ('Applications submitted without prior approval of an exception will be deemed ineligible'). CFF grants@cff.org, or Mike Carlino (MCarlino@cff.org) for RFA technicals — ask to be put on the Funding Opportunities Newsletter so you get the December date the day it posts. BWF cams@bwfund.org for institutional-eligibility questions. NJCCR njccr@doh.nj.gov — and note their pre-award Technical Assistance meeting is MANDATORY. Blood Cancer United researchprograms@bloodcancerunited.org (not the older lls.org address still shown on stale pages). HHMI FHS@hhmi.org after the August 2027 status notification. ALS Association: join the ALS research email list, which is where RFAs are announced. Attend the free NIH LRP technical-assistance webinar on 6 October 2026.

Your referees — one conversation, early, covering the whole year rather than one application. Three to five letters recur across nearly everything, and the constraints differ: NIH needs 3–5 submitted by the referees through eRA Commons BY the due date and your sponsor does NOT count toward the three; Damon Runyon needs three, one of which MUST be your thesis advisor and none of which may be your sponsor; NSF PRFB needs exactly two, in BEFORE you submit, and not your sponsor; NASA NPP needs one from your thesis advisor if you are within five years of the degree, and explicitly NOT from the NASA advisor; AHA needs three 4-page reports uploaded by the referees before you can submit.
materials_to_gather: NIH Biographical Sketch via SciENcv, plus an ORCID iD. Slow the first time, reusable forever. ORCID is a hard requirement for the F32 and, since 1 September 2026, for the LRP. Note the K/F biosketch is 5 pages in the legacy format; the Common Form has no hard page limit but is shaped by SciENcv's own data entry.

A one-page Specific Aims. This is the master asset: it becomes the NSF 1-page Project Summary, the spine of a 5-page Damon Runyon proposal, the LRP research description, and the thing you email a programme officer for a five-minute read.

Research narrative at four lengths, because the page limits are administratively enforced and differ sharply: 12 pages for the NIH K-series — and this is the most commonly misstated number in the whole system, because 'Candidate Information and Goals for Career Development' and 'Research Strategy' share ONE combined 12-page limit, not 12 each; 6 pages for the F32 Research Training Project Strategy, NSF PRFB, ALS Safenowitz, and MSCRF; 5 pages for Damon Runyon (single-spaced, 12-point, figures inside the limit, references outside), HHMI Hanna Gray (text, figures and legends inside 5 pages, reference list outside), AHA, and BWF CASI; 10 pages for NSF AAPF; 7 pages for CFF and Breakthrough T1D; 15 DOUBLE-SPACED pages for NASA NPP, which will return a non-conforming proposal unreviewed.

The sponsor/mentor package — the slowest thing you do not control. F32 Sponsor Commitment 6 pages; NIH K mentor and co-mentor plans 6 pages; NSF Sponsoring Scientist Statement 3 pages; Damon Runyon sponsor training plan 2 pages PLUS a mentorship track record covering graduate and postdoctoral trainees from the past 10 years PLUS a separate sponsor letter; AHA training plan 3 pages plus a past-and-current-trainees list 3 pages; NASA NPP advisor recommendation, which is a gate rather than a document. Request these 8–10 weeks out.

Reference letters as a standing asset — a short roster of four people, briefed once on your year's plan, with the per-funder rules written down (see WHO TO TALK TO). Budget for the fact that several portals will not let you SUBMIT until the letters are in (Damon Runyon, AHA, NSF PRFB).

Institutional letters, which route through people who are slow in August and December: the AAPF host-institution letter with two signatures; the NJCCR letter of institutional/organizational support; CDMRP's Letter of Eligibility (missing it is an automatic-rejection ground for PRP EIRA Funding Level 1); the APS Blewett letter of institutional support; BWF CASI's Signing Official e-signature, for which 'Extensions will not be given for missing institutional signatures.'

Transcripts and degree evidence. NASA NPP requires them for Postdoctoral Fellow applicants only, as PDFs under 10 MB, with SSN, date and place of birth, parents' names and student ID REDACTED from every page of every document. Damon Runyon wants a copy of the diploma (a letter substitute is allowed for a defended-but-not-yet-conferred PhD). DAAD wants transcripts of ALL university studies.

Budget — mostly a non-issue at this stage, which is worth knowing so you don't over-prepare. BWF CASI requires no budget at either stage; NSF fellowships are fixed-amount ($110,000/yr AAPF and PRFB, $190,000 total MSPRF); F32 stipends follow the NRSA scale. Where a budget IS required, the rules are what kill applications: no indirect costs at all on the ALS Safenowitz or the MSCRF postdoc fellowship; NJCCR 15% inclusive; USDA AFRI a $3,000/yr institutional allowance in lieu of indirects, with 'Requests exceeding budgetary guidelines will not be reviewed.'

A one-page lay / public abstract. Increasingly required and increasingly public: CDMRP lay abstract (1 page), Blood Cancer United Lay Description (2,000–2,500 characters, and the Summary is capped at 500), MSCRF's 1,800-character non-confidential summary flagged 'If awarded, this information becomes public', BWF PDEP's lay abstract — for which BWF publishes five full worked examples — and the ADA and Damon Runyon public abstracts.

Memberships and registrations that are eligibility gates, not conveniences: AHA Professional Membership for YOU and your mentor, active at submission, 3–5 days to process; ASM membership at application and 'remain active through the meeting' for the travel award; ISTAART for the Alzheimer's two-day extension; APS membership (the portal lists it as a starting condition even though the Blewett page does not — an unresolved conflict worth an email to honors@aps.org).

An AI-use disclosure statement. AHA requires disclosure at submission and may administratively withdraw a proposal where undisclosed use is identified; HHMI, HFSP, ADA (on institutional letterhead, signed by you and your Research Officer) and Luce/ACLS all ask for it. Write it once.
mechanisms_that_matter_most: NIH K99/R00 Pathway to Independence — the award that changes your job market. 12 Oct 2026 published / Tue 13 Oct 2026 operative; then 12 Feb 2027, which is the last new date before the parent NOFOs expire 8 May 2027. Hard gate: no more than 4 years of postdoctoral research training AT THE TIME OF INITIAL APPLICATION OR RESUBMISSION. NCI does not participate. Three parent NOFOs (PA-24-193 clinical trial required, PA-24-194 not allowed, PA-24-195 BESH required).

NIH F32 Parent NRSA Individual Postdoctoral Fellowship (PA-25-423) — 8 Dec 2026, then 8 Apr and 8 Aug 2027, 5 p.m. local. Resubmissions fall on the SAME dates, not a month later. US citizenship / national status / permanent residence required; 3-year aggregate NRSA postdoctoral cap including T32 time.

NIH Loan Repayment Program (Extramural LRP) — 19 Nov 2026, 11:59 p.m. EST. Open now. No NIH grant required. Two-year contract starting 1 July 2027. The best effort-to-value ratio on this entire list for anyone with qualifying educational debt. Disqualifier: any research funding or salary from a for-profit organisation.

NSF Postdoctoral Research Fellowships in Biology (PRFB, NSF 26-504) — 29 Sept 2026, then 28 Sept 2027. $110,000/yr for two years, ~75 awards. Lifetime cap of TWO submissions, ever, so do not burn one on a rushed attempt.

NSF Astronomy & Astrophysics Postdoctoral Fellowships (AAPF, NSF 22-621) — submission WINDOW 15 Aug – 15 Oct 2026, annually thereafter. $110,000/yr for 36 months. Lifetime cap of two competitions; withdrawn or returned-without-review proposals do not count.

NSF Mathematical Sciences Postdoctoral Research Fellowships (MSPRF, NSF 23-603) — 21 Oct 2026, third Wednesday in October annually. $190,000 over 48 months; one proposal per person per year; self-submitted.

NASA Postdoctoral Program (NPP) — 1 Nov 2026, 6:00 p.m. ET, then typically 1 March and 1 July (the Astrobiology Program skips the July round). The one NASA mechanism where the dates are stable enough to plan against. The Center advisor's recommendation is a gate.

HHMI Hanna H. Gray Fellows — 15 Dec 2026, 11:59 p.m. ET. Biennial. Eligibility questionnaire live since 15 Sept 2026 and required before the form opens. Funds both the postdoc and the faculty phases. Other funding does not stop you applying; HHMI adjudicates at offer.

Damon Runyon Fellowship — 15 March 2027, portal opens 15 Jan 2027. The strictest entry rules on the list (no prior accepted postdoc fellowship, no NIH K, an 18-month degree window and a 12-month sponsor-lab window, both computed from the deadline) and per-sponsor caps you must check before writing.
EMBO Postdoctoral Fellowships — year-round submission, next cutoff 22 Jan 2027, 14:00 CET. Eligibility runs off your SUBMISSION date. From immediately after that cutoff, one application per lifetime.

HFSP Long-Term and Cross-Disciplinary Fellowships — LOI early May, invited full proposal late September, 9:00 a.m. ET; AY2028 dates unpublished. One HFSP fellowship per lifetime; host supervisor may endorse only one LOI per year; requires a change of country, and for CDF a change of discipline.

Burroughs Wellcome Career Award at the Scientific Interface (CASI) — LOI mid-August, invited full proposal 11 Jan 2027. Bars K99 holders and acceptors; explicitly allows K01 holders. Funds postdoc plus faculty phases.

AHA Postdoctoral Fellowship — projected first week of August 2027, 3:00 p.m. CT. Membership for you and your mentor is an eligibility gate; no late submissions and no appeals; maximum four years of AHA postdoctoral support per person.

Blood Cancer United (LLS) Career Development Program, Fellow and Special Fellow — OPEN: eligibility gate 15 Oct 2026, LOI 1 Nov, full application and three blind references 15 Nov, all 3:00 p.m. ET. Concurrency is a VALUE test with a K99 carve-out, not a named-award list.

Disease- and state-specific fellowships worth a look if they match your topic: Breakthrough T1D (~1–2 July), CFF (May and December), ALS Safenowitz (RFA → LOI exactly 5 weeks → full proposal 9–12 weeks), Alzheimer's AARFA (LOI mid-August), ADA Pathway Initiator (institution-nominated), MSCRF Maryland (mid-January only), NJCCR New Jersey (mandatory TA meeting + mandatory LOI in December), TRDRP California (LOI late August), CIRM California (apply to a host programme, no citizenship requirement).

Not a grant, but real money and real jobs: NIST PREP postdoc positions (rolling at Gaithersburg, ~14–47 day windows at Boulder) and NIH T32 slots (an appointment your programme makes; US citizens, nationals and permanent residents only).
where_to_find_examples: NIH's curated samples index is the single best resource and is uneven — know the gaps before you hunt. VERIFIED ABSENT: no F32, no K25, no K43, no LRP sample exists anywhere on it. VERIFIED PRESENT and worth the time: NIA publishes ONE applicant's K99/R00 A0 AND A1 with both summary statements ('received an excellent score and was funded upon resubmission') — the A0-to-A1 pairing is the whole teaching value; the page returns HTTP 405 to a plain fetch and 200 to a browser. NIAID publishes a K23 (Friedman-Klabanoff, 'Serological markers of natural immunity to Plasmodium falciparum infection') with full application and summary statement, plus K01 and K08 samples. NHGRI's ELSI page publishes several paired K01 applications and summary statements (Sabatello, Prince, Lazaro-Munoz, Yu) plus K99/R00 samples.

NSF: use the awards API, not the human search UI, which returns 'Search Results (0)' to a non-rendering fetch. api.nsf.gov/services/v1/awards.json?fundProgramName=MSPRF returns the funded cohort with titles, PIs, amounts and programme officers. Every AAPF title begins 'Postdoctoral Fellowship: AAPF:' and every PRFB title 'Postdoctoral Fellowship: PRFB:', so the titles alone are a clean, complete corpus of what got funded.

Foundation abstract libraries that genuinely substitute for samples: Damon Runyon's current-projects page filtered to Fellow gives a 150–200-word lay abstract, title, institution, cancer type and the NAMED SPONSOR for each Fellow — it doubles as a who-to-talk-to index. Pew's Directory of Fellows gives an abstract plus the fellow's institutional email, lab URL, mentor name and country of origin, filterable, and Pew explicitly endorses using it to find a sponsor. The ALS Association's Funded Grants Database on ProposalCentral opens with NO login and filters to 'Milton Safenowitz Postdoctoral Fellowship Program'. MSCRF's Annual Report PDF (not the awardees page) prints per awardee: name, institution, mentor, disease target, amount, title and a full funded abstract. Blood Cancer United's research-we-fund page and TRDRP's funded-research database do the same.

Real worked DOCUMENTS, which are rarer than abstracts and much more useful: BWF publishes a PDEP-specific PDF containing five full worked LAY ABSTRACTS. HHMI puts redacted real applications inside ARC, behind the eligibility questionnaire. Luce/ACLS publishes a sample application for each China Studies variant, current cycle. RSF publishes three sample Visiting Scholar proposals, which share the exact format spec with the Visiting Researcher track. CDMRP publishes component templates in eBRAP. NIH publishes the Table of Page Limits, the Biographical Sketch Common Form and format pages for data-management and other plans.

Where no sample exists, use the published RUBRIC instead — several funders print the criteria reviewers actually score: NASA NPP's 40/20/20/20 weighting and its ≥75-of-100 selectability threshold; HFSP's published scoring guide for reviewers; APS Blewett's seven selection criteria (which read as a de facto rubric for a career-return application); ADA's review criteria; Blood Cancer United's Mission Score / Priority Score machinery, including that Mission Scores of 4 or 5 are eliminated without full review; TRDRP's NIH-style 1–9 scale.

Named review panels, which are the closest thing to a study-section roster outside NIH: BWF publishes its CASI and CAMS Advisory Committee members; APS names the Blewett selection committee; NSF names the cognizant programme officer on every award record.

HONEST NEGATIVES, verified rather than assumed — do not send yourself hunting: no published sample application exists for the NIH F32, K25, K43 or LRP; NASA NPP; NIST PREP; EMBO; HFSP; Simons Junior Fellows; ASM travel awards; SfN NSP; Fulbright; DAAD; AHA (you see your own critiques in ProposalCentral and nobody else's); CFF; NJCCR; CDMRP (component templates yes, a full funded application no); or BWF generally, apart from the PDEP lay abstracts. Several of these publish funded titles or lay abstracts only — useful for calibration, not a model of an application.

For NIST PREP specifically: prep.umd.edu lists ~200 project postings with sponsor name, research summary, position category and start date. It is the richest public picture of what a NIST sponsor actually asks for and the right place to learn the house style — but it is an archive, not a vacancy board, so apply only through a hub's live system.
common_mistakes: Reading a stale funder page as an open call. This is the single most common failure and it is the funders' fault, not yours. ACLS still displayed 'Competition Status: Accepting Applications Now' the day AFTER its deadline passed. The AHA page is headed '2027 Postdoctoral Fellowship' while carrying a deadline that has already gone. CFF's clinical postdoc page today still shows a December 2025 date. Breakthrough T1D still displays 'FY27 Training Awards — Full Proposals due 2 July 2026'. The APS Blewett page says 'Nominations are open' in its header and 'Nominations are currently closed' in the award card on the same page. Rule: trust the RFA/NOFO/Guidelines document over the landing page, and when the two disagree, the RFA governs.

Reading an aggregator's rolled-forward date. 'December 12, 2026' circulates for the CFF postdoc fellowship; it is a SATURDAY, appears on no CFF page, and is 12 December 2024 (a real Thursday deadline) with the year bumped. The Grants.gov card for the USDA AFRI EWD NOFO shows 31 December 2026, which is the NOFO-wide envelope and is eight months adrift from the A7201 postdoc row. Always land on the funder's own document.

Missing the real front door, which is usually not called a deadline. You cannot reach the Blood Cancer United LOI without passing the Eligibility Phase (15 Oct 2026). The HHMI application form does not open to you without the ARC questionnaire. CDMRP's pre-application is mandatory and its absence is an automatic-rejection ground even though it is never screened. NJCCR has a MANDATORY technical-assistance meeting and a mandatory LOI, and the LOI is what generates your portal account. BWF CAMS gates the full application behind an eligibility check. TRDRP's LOI is a competitive screen — no more than 80 pre/postdoctoral LOIs are invited forward. Alzheimer's AARFA: 'Full applications will not be accepted without an approved LOI from the current cycle.'

Blowing the K99 clock by treating the resubmission as free. The 4-year limit is measured at the due date of the RESUBMISSION too, and the A1 cannot be filed before the A0's summary statement issues (~5 months), which is what forces an October A0 into a July A1 rather than March. An A0 filed at 46 months is a single shot. Separately, if you achieve independence — any faculty or non-mentored research position — before the K99 is made, neither the K99 nor the R00 will be issued.

Accepting the wrong award first. Damon Runyon is permanently closed to anyone who has already accepted another postdoctoral fellowship, and to NIH K holders. BWF CASI excludes K99 holders and acceptors while explicitly allowing K01. ADA Pathway Initiator bars a concurrent K99/R00 and allows every other career-development award. Breakthrough T1D and the ALS Safenowitz bar a concurrent postdoctoral fellowship. EMBO and HFSP bar concurrent salaried employment or another paid fellowship. Apply everywhere; sequence acceptances deliberately.

Assuming NIH's '5 p.m. local time' applies everywhere. Real deviations that have cost people a cycle: NASA NPP 6:00 p.m. ET (not the 11:59 p.m. ROSES habit — six hours gone); NIH LRP 11:59 p.m. EASTERN fixed for everyone regardless of where you are; SfN NSP noon Eastern; Simons noon ET; HFSP 9:00 a.m. ET; AHA 3:00 p.m. CENTRAL; BWF 3:00 p.m. ET with the submit button graying out and never reactivating; Blood Cancer United 3:00 p.m. ET; ALS Association 1:00 p.m. ET (changed from 5 p.m.); TRDRP 12:00 noon PACIFIC; DAAD midnight CET = 6 p.m. EST; EMBO 14:00 CET; NSF 'submitting organisation's local time' which, for a self-submitted fellowship, is the address on your Research.gov profile — not where you are sitting, and it needs 21 days to change.

Letting the letters sink you. NSF PRFB references must be submitted BEFORE you submit your proposal. Damon Runyon will not let you submit until all three are uploaded. AHA requires three 4-page reference reports uploaded by the referees first. NIH will not review an application with fewer than the required number of letters, and your sponsor does not count toward the three. LRP letters, mentor letter and IBO certification are all due at the deadline with no grace. The one case where later is fine: HHMI's mentor questionnaire is due three weeks AFTER your own submission.

Page-limit and formatting errors that are administratively fatal rather than merely scored. The K-series 12 pages is 'Candidate Information and Goals for Career Development' AND 'Research Strategy' COMBINED — the most commonly misstated number in the system. The Introduction to a Resubmission is 1 page for fellowships and K awards (research grants get 3; T32 resubmissions get 3). NASA NPP: 'your proposal may be returned without review if it does not conform to these formatting instructions.' CDMRP silently DELETES over-length pages before review. CFF will not review an over-length research plan. MSCRF, TRDRP, NJCCR and Blood Cancer United all administratively reject for format or altered line spacing. BWF rejects for more than three reprints or any unrequested supplemental material.

Treating 'no prior-award bar' as 'no bar at all'. CDMRP, NSF AAPF and MSPRF, TRDRP, MSCRF, NJCCR and AARFA have no NIH-style prior-funding exclusion — but every one has a hard career-stage clock measured at a specific date, and several carry SPONSOR-SIDE caps that disqualify you through no fault of your own: Damon Runyon (one application per sponsor per session, maximum two concurrent Fellows), HFSP (one LOI endorsement per host supervisor per year), Pew (one applicant per sponsor per year), AHA (a mentor may supervise no more than four AHA-funded fellows). Ask your PI before you write, not after.

Mis-filing yourself into the wrong mechanism. The Fogarty K43 excludes US citizens, permanent residents and anyone based at a US institution. ARPA-E IGNIITE requires a pre-tenure tenure-track faculty appointment at a US institution, with the FAQ stating 'exceptions will not be considered' — it is not a postdoc route. NIST PREP is a job advert, not a competition. CIRM Scholars is an application to one of 18 host programmes, not to CIRM. T32 is an appointment, not an application. USDA AFRI requires the A7201 code in the NIFA Supplemental Information Form and the FAS programme code in the ABSTRACT — putting the FAS code in the form risks being 'returned without review'.

Waiting for a date that has not been published, instead of setting a watch. As of 2026-09-18 there is genuinely no published next date for the AHA postdoc fellowship, BWF PDEP, Pew LAF, Simons Junior Fellows, ASM travel awards, HFSP AY2028, APS Blewett 2027, the USDA AFRI postdoc fellowship, or IGNIITE 2027. The correct response is a watch route, not a guess: newsletters (ALS Association research list, CFF Funding Opportunities Newsletter), a saved job search (NIST PREP Boulder), a calendar reminder on the month the funder historically posts (Pew's FAQ February–May; AFRI January–May; BWF PDEP early October; MSCRF late October), and an email to the programme office.
